A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same accountability-modeling research. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and all equations, figures and tables can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original DST experiments on MultiWOZ and Snips, threshold and loss-weight analyses, and GPT-4o mini user-simulation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including benchmark results, ablations, user-simulation outcomes and appendix validation results.

M1.justification: The accountability head, joint training objective, dialogue-state correction algorithm and user-confirmation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds inference documentation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MultiWOZ 2.4 for multi-turn DST and Snips for single-turn slot prediction, with the same user-simulation scenario. No dataset, domain or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: The comparator membership remains unchanged across Tables 2–4, Figure 3 and Table 7. Table 3 retains GPT-4o, IC-DST, OrchestraLLM, CorrectionLM and the same supervised baselines.

E3.justification: The specified splits, backbone sizes, training settings, thresholds and simulator prompts remain unchanged. Section 4.2's added FPR/FNR formulas spell out the existing turn-based metrics; Appendix A.2 discloses inference details rather than revising a previously stated protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an informal model-size sensitivity observation: smaller models performed worse, while larger models encountered resource constraints. No configurations or scores accompany it. The existing threshold and loss-weight ablations, oracle analysis and five correction cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state in Appendix A.2 that belief states are generated using a single run. Neither adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All matched numerical table entries and Figure 3 curves are unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly reports lower performance from smaller models and that all generated outputs conformed to JSON without formatting errors; these are additional qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. The added FPR/FNR formulas restate metrics already defined in words, and no theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about error detection, approximately three-point JGA improvement, 70.51 JGA after self-correction, and user confirmations' potential to reduce overreliance.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly assumes cooperative users and acknowledges simulator limitations, then newly interprets Table 7 as a lower bound for achievable performance with cooperative users. Section 8 and Appendix A.2 add deployment and model-size tradeoff arguments, including cost-effectiveness excluding training overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies inference without oracle belief states, no JSON-enforcing post-processing, and an empty-dictionary fallback for formatting failures. It also explains model-size selection under resource constraints. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, training times, prompts and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Dey and Desarkar (2024) to connect the auxiliary prediction objective with keyword-guided dialogue generation, and Dey et al. (2022) to the evaluation discussion. The main related-work section remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands the introductory example and selected discussion and appendix paragraphs, adds cross-references, corrects 'Dialogue Sate' and updates an author email. The overall section organization and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption is rewritten, Algorithm 1 and several displays are repositioned, and the example table has adjusted column widths. The loss-weight and example tables exchange numbers 5 and 6. All three figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through explicit error-rate counting, inference inputs, formatting-failure handling and simulator assumptions. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. These documentation gains are qualified by new lower-bound and cost-effectiveness interpretations that lack direct human-user or cost-comparison evidence.
